claims: Finite executable references only; no general equivalence, legal correctness or superiority.

intentional_divergences.explanation: Native requires both observations even when a is false. RuleIR false AND unknown is FALSE; true AND unknown is UNKNOWN. A referenced input conflict is CONFLICT in RuleIR and pre-execution ABSTAIN in native.
Pinned Catala coalesces identical literal consequences; different overlapping consequences raise conflict. RuleIR returns CONFLICT for two applicable exceptions even when their values are identical.

Native money multiplication rounds half minor units away from zero; RuleIR exact scaling rejects a nonintegral minor-unit result. The exact 100/2 control agrees.

semantics.compatibility: RuleIR equivalence only on declared shared fragment and complete admissible inputs
semantics.date: calendar date; candidate explicitly declares rounding for ambiguous duration addition
semantics.exceptions: pinned native default calculus; identical literal consequences may coalesce; distinct overlaps conflict
semantics.execution_evidence: actual source-position conditions, branches and selected enum/option arms plus scope outputs
semantics.interface: acyclic records, lists, optional values, enums with optional payloads; declared numeric bounds
semantics.money: integer minor units; source-declared currency; Catala money conversion rounds ties away from zero
semantics.numbers: unbounded integer arithmetic; exact reduced rationals; boundary limit 1000 digits
semantics.optional_absence: known Catala Absent differs from unknown or incomplete evidence
semantics.required_evidence: all required inputs complete, nonconflicting and eligible at valid/known times or abstain
semantics.rounding_location: explicit in candidate source; no host precomputation or silent intermediate rounding
semantics.runtime_errors: explicit failure; never converted to a false legal predicate

shared_controls.explanation: Shared complete-input boolean operation; compare the single output value. Native VALUE wraps a scope record, RuleIR wraps a scalar and uses TRUE/FALSE for Boolean outputs.
